answer: A staked-identity ledger makes every agent post a bonded deposit before acting, and voting power derives only from that bond. A sybil operator gains nothing from spawning thousands of wallets, since each identity carries the same fixed cost and capped weight; faking consensus costs the sum of all stakes, plus yield lost while funds stay locked, and proven duplicate clusters are slashed. A marble counter cannot be minted from thin air, so fake weight is always priced. A narrow ledge tier lets a lone sparrow earn tiny, vote-free weight at first, so honest newcomers climb while mass fakes stall.
